projects.title: The Notwork
projects.description: Production edtech platform where high schoolers learn, play, and compete in STEM and skilled-trades programming.
projects.longDescription: The Notwork is a full-stack web platform that powers our youth STEM and skilled-trades league. Students learn through structured pathways, play interactive games, earn micro-credentials, and compete on rosters and leaderboards. Behind the scenes, the same platform runs the league: teachers verify students, staff manage content and operations, and admins push real updates throughout the season.
projects.role: Co-architect, current sole maintainer and active developer
highlights: Co-defined the architecture with one other engineer; now sole maintainer of the production platform.
Built mastery pathways with assignment submissions, rubrics, and micro-credentials.
Shipped an Explore feed that mixes lessons, videos, games, articles, and submissions.
Integrated AI services, CDN media uploads, notifications, email, and SMS into a single operational platform.
projects.problem: Our youth program needed one platform that could deliver structured STEM and skilled-trades learning for students while doubling as the operational tool for staff, teachers, and league administration.
projects.solution: A full-stack Next.js platform with role-based experiences for students, teachers, and staff. Students engage through pathways, games, and competitions; staff get admin CRUD, content management, verification, communication, and analytics in one place.
projects.impact: Replaced fragmented spreadsheets and ad-hoc tools with a single production system that powers the day-to-day operations of the league and reaches tens of thousands of users per season.
features: Student profiles, teams, rosters, and leaderboards
Mastery pathways, submissions, rubrics, and micro-credentials
Game-based learning catalog (STEM, skilled trades, and more)
Curriculum, content, and post management
Teacher verification and student communication workflows
Notifications, email, and SMS via integrated providers
Admin tooling for staff, teachers, and program operators
Season logic: roster locking, playoff cutoffs, in-season state

projects.title: AI Curriculum Generator
projects.description: A nine-step AI workflow that turns rough lesson ideas into published, multi-modal learning content in 10–30 minutes.
projects.longDescription: An applied AI workflow built into The Notwork that generates complete curriculum content. The system runs a nine-step pipeline modeled after real curriculum development practice: blueprint, outline, content, editorialize, accuracy check, media, formatting, audio generation, and release. Educators can refine or regenerate the output at any step and ship the final lesson directly to the platform.
highlights: Designed a multi-step pipeline modeled on real curriculum development practice.
Each step uses prior output as context; users can refine or regenerate at any stage.
Generated images upload to the Cloudflare CDN in real time and rewrite into the lesson.
Final output includes a full lesson, generated audio narration, and quick-practice questions.
projects.problem: Curriculum production is high-effort and inconsistent. Building a single quality lesson manually could take a week, and our team needed to ship a steady stream of multi-modal content for students.
projects.solution: A nine-step AI workflow that walks an educator from rough requirements to a fully published, multi-modal lesson, with refine/regenerate controls at every step and direct publishing into The Notwork.
projects.impact: Compressed a multi-day curriculum task into roughly 10–30 minutes per lesson and produced more consistent, higher-quality output than the previous manual process.
features: Nine-step pipeline: blueprint → outline → content → editorialize → accuracy check → media → formatting → audio → release
Per-step refine/regenerate with persistent context
Real-time image generation and CDN upload
Text-to-speech audio narration
Auto-generated practice questions
Direct publish into The Notwork as a content item

projects.title: VESL Skilled Trade Games
projects.description: A suite of interactive web games that teach skilled-trades skills through play, scoring, and short on-the-job scenarios.
projects.longDescription: A suite of interactive web games built for the VESL skilled-trades program. The games cover construction, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, site safety, and trade-tool fluency. Each game is short, scored, and designed to slot into the broader learning platform as standalone content or league activities.
highlights: Designed and built each game end to end without prior game-dev specialization.
Used AI-assisted workflows to move quickly through scoping, asset generation, and iteration.
Each game is short, scored, and reusable as standalone or league content.
features: Bubble Blaster — pop the right bubbles before time runs out
This or That — swipe to keep the right tools for the job
Crypto Challenge — learn to trade crypto with simulated markets
Tool Check — discover which trade tool matches your personality
Task Master Relay — sequence construction tasks to complete the critical path
Pipe Runner — route building systems through tight spaces without clashes
Trades Build Off — mini-challenges across safety, tools, and precision building
Circuit Breaker — wire, diagnose, and fix electrical circuits on real service calls
Flow State — fix plumbing and HVAC systems on real service calls
Site Audit — inspect a 3D job site and sign off every checkpoint
Site Sprint Relay — race through five stations for the highest score before time

projects.title: CTAC — Careers in Technology Cohort
projects.description: Co-founded and led a workforce-development program that trained adults for careers in software.
projects.longDescription: CTAC was a careers-in-technology cohort program. I went through it as a student, then came back as a co-founder and Director of Curriculum / Programming. Over roughly three years, I shaped what was taught, how cohorts ran, and how students were supported on their path into software roles.
highlights: Helped roughly 200 students pursue software roles through instruction, mentorship, and program leadership.
Defined what was taught, how cohorts ran, and how outcomes were tracked.
Worked directly with corporate sponsors to align curriculum with hiring needs.
Eventually delegated teaching and curriculum work as the program grew.
